# 🪑 The Desk Is Back: Why Some Offices Are Quietly Bringing Back Assigned Seats

A desk with your name on it is returning to some offices.

After the pandemic, many workplaces started using **hot-desking**. In this system, workers do not have their own desks. They choose any free desk when they arrive.

The system can save space. But some employees have not been happy with it.

They say the office can feel less comfortable than working from home. They may sit next to people they do not know. They may also have to search for a suitable desk every morning.

Now, some companies are quietly changing direction.

They are bringing back **assigned desks**, at least for some workers or some teams. Several companies, including Scotiabank and iCapital Network, have discussed this move.

The change does not mean that every office is returning to the old system. It means that some offices are reducing their use of hot-desking.

The question is simple:

**Does having your own place help you feel more connected and ready to work?**

## A desk can feel like more than furniture

One workplace survey found a clear connection. Workers with assigned desks were more likely to say that they felt they belonged at work. The figure was **87%**, compared with **74%** among workers without assigned desks.

They were also more likely to say they could focus well. This is a connection, not proof that the desk itself caused the better feeling. Still, it shows why some employees want a stable place at work.

## A small return inside a bigger shift

Assigned desks may be coming back in some offices, but the larger office trend is still moving toward shared space.

A business property survey found that companies with one desk or less for each employee fell from **56% in 2023 to 40% in 2024**. The companies surveyed expected that number to fall to about **one in three by 2026**.

So, this is not a full return to the old office. It is a selective change. Some teams may get their own desks, while other parts of the same company continue to share.

## In one line…

Hot-desking is still growing across many offices, but some companies are learning that flexibility does not always feel like belonging.

# The Quiet Return of the Desk with a Name on It

For a while, many modern offices had no home base.

After the pandemic, **hot-desking** became more common. In this system, workers do not have their own desks. They choose an empty desk when they arrive.

Now, that system is facing complaints.

Some employees do not like searching for a desk each morning. Others do not enjoy sitting beside different people every day. They also want a work area that feels more stable and predictable.

So, in some offices, the assigned desk is coming back.

Companies such as Scotiabank and iCapital Network are quietly reducing their use of hot-desking. For some teams, one desk is once again kept for one worker.

But this is not a full return across the business world.

Desk sharing is still common. A 2024 office survey found that the share of companies with at least one desk for each worker fell from 56% in 2023 to 40% in 2024. The companies surveyed expected that figure to fall to about one third by 2026.

The office is changing in two directions at once.

### A small desk can create a big feeling

A workplace survey found that workers with assigned desks were more likely to say they felt they belonged at work. They were also more likely to say they could focus well. This shows a connection, but it does not prove that the desk itself caused these better feelings.

### A mixed model is taking shape

The wider trend still favors shared space. At the same time, some companies are bringing back fixed seats for selected workers or teams. This suggests that offices may not choose one system for everyone. They may use shared desks in some areas and assigned desks in others.

## In one line…

The assigned desk is quietly returning in some offices, but hot-desking is still part of the larger workplace trend. The future office may be a careful mix of personal space and shared space.
